a holistic approach to targeting nanoparticles can be used to increase the efficacy of nanomedicins.
nanoparticles must be administered via the optimal route, must be designed to avoid off-target interactions and must be designed for controlled release.
the design of nanomedicine should consider the route of administration and temporal control of nanoparticles to improve therapeutic efficacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of polymeric nanoparticles for the treatment of cancer and other diseases.
developing new materials for biomedical applications, with a focus on nanotechnology.
the development of novel nanoscale systems for the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of human disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nanomedicines should be designed to target disease, not cells or tissues, to achieve the ultimate goal of improving clinical outcomes.
a holistic approach to targeting is required to achieve the full potential of nanoparticles in medicine.
the field of targeted nanomedicine has been successful in the development of new technologies that have the potential to revolutionize the practice of medicine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing nanoparticles that can be injected intravenously and that are designed to be taken up by macrophages, which are then used to deliver drugs to the brain.
we developed a novel platform technology that is capable of achieving the desired biodistribution of nanoparticles, which in turn can be used for the delivery of therapeutics and diagnostics.
we have developed a new approach for the design of targeted nanoparticles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of nanoparticles should be guided by the clinical context in which they will be used.
the route of administration is a critical variable for the design of nanoparticles.
a holistic approach to nanoparticle targeting must be considered when designing nanomedicines.
